_about: Announced U.S. job cuts by month and the part employers attributed to artificial intelligence, from Challenger, Gray & Christmas's monthly reports (Table 4, job cuts by reason, and the month-by-month table). Hand-kept for the AI labor panel (AI Economy → Dark Output; server/aiLabor.js). Add a month when a report is published: totalCuts, aiCuts, the year-to-date AI figure the report states, and its link. Nothing here names a company.
notes: All monthly figures are from Challenger, Gray & Christmas's own releases: Table 4 ('Job Cuts by Reason') and the month-by-month table of each monthly PDF, cross-checked against the blog post text; no month relies on press coverage. For January-March 2025 the PDFs were not located, so totals come from the blog posts and the later month-by-month table, and the AI zero is derived from later tables (see row notes). Monthly AI figures reconcile exactly with each stated YTD. Definition: 'Artificial Intelligence' is the reason an employer gives in its layoff announcement; Challenger has tracked it as a distinct reason since May 2023 and counts announced plans, not realized separations. 'Technological Update (possibly AI)' is used 'when a company states new technology was the main reason for layoffs and AI is alluded to but not directly tied to the cuts' (July 2026 report); in 2026 a separate 'Technological Update (automation)' row also appears (1,353, all in February 2026). techUpdateCuts here is the 'possibly AI' row only; a blank table cell is recorded as 0. Revisions seen: (1) the 20,000 'Technological Update (possibly AI)' cuts first appear in the May 2025 report's YTD column with no monthly entry, having been moved out of Restructuring; they are not assigned to a month. (2) Through the June 2025 report AI was described as a subset of Technological Update ('Of these, 75 were explicitly attributed to Artificial Intelligence'); from July 2025 the two are reported side by side. (3) The November 2025 report was reissued to correct a year-to-date comparison (not the AI figures). (4) Challenger notes that some reductions are announced as ranges or over several years and that attribution is ambiguous (July 2026 report). Since-2023 cumulative AI totals stated by Challenger: 71,825 (end 2025), 193,226 (October 2026).

loadedCostPerJob.why: An assumption, not a measurement. The average U.S. private-sector job costs an employer on the order of $100,000 a year in pay and benefits; the cuts employers tie to AI are concentrated in technology and professional roles, which cost more. $150,000 is the middle used here, with $100,000 and $250,000 as the range. Change it here.
